question: Do the simplex cutout fixes outside N06.4's domain, router.java_quirks.cutout_hole_crosses_border=false (the stand-in division line of a corner on the outer border no longer clips later pieces, so no piece of a hole crossing the border vanishes) and router.java_quirks.simplex_octagon_half_corner=false (a corner that is not an integer point and lies on no outer border line is divided at its exact point, so the pieces beside it no longer overlap), each alone and both, keep the unrouted total within N02's totals rule (accept no-regress: correctness fixes) of Java's cutouts, with no via in a pad, no copper below the minimum and no new clearance or DRC error; do the 45 degree rows keep Java's sessions byte for byte; and how often does a run reach the two switches?

pairs_rule: the verdict pair is judged by the totals block with the hard and guard metrics below; the reported pairs are the switch-by-switch bisection (N06's decisions: one switch per bug), run up front. On the two 45 degree rows (fixtures/Issue026-J2_reference.dsn, canary-pwr) every arm must show session_differences 0 and both reach counters 0; either failing is a bug in N06.14's diff or in its reach claim, not a verdict

boards.eligibility: every row; no row is dropped after a number. Chosen before any routed number: the switches reach a drill page only in any-angle mode, so A07's three any-angle variants (the boards N06.12 registered for any-angle mode) are the measured rows; two 45 degree boards of n06-g.txt check that nothing changes where the switches are not reached; canary-pwr also goes through the KiCad plugin path (plugin_canary)

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: freerouting-dev gate collect's count on the imported SES; plugin canary: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py
metric_definitions.below_minimum: the nets with copper under their class width in freerouting-dev widths <DSN> <SES> (under_mm > 0); plugin canary: KiCad track_width errors
metric_definitions.clearance_violations: the router's clearance violations of the final board (RESULT board_statistics; gate collect's clearance_violations)
metric_definitions.drc_real: plugin canary only: KiCad error-severity items other than unconnected items
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: plugin canary only: KiCad's unconnected items after the import (canary grade.sh); the totals signal where it is a number
metric_definitions.unrouted: gate collect's unrouted (connections.incomplete_count) of the final board; the totals signal of the DSN rows, which have no KiCad board
metric_definitions.session_differences: n06_run.py: 1 when the arm's SES differs from the baseline's
metric_definitions.cutout_hole_crosses_border_reached: STATS total.counts.cutout_hole_crosses_border_reached: the simplex cutout pieces whose first-division-line clip differs between the two arms of the switch, counted in both arms
metric_definitions.simplex_octagon_half_corner_reached: STATS total.counts.simplex_octagon_half_corner_reached: the simplex cutout corners that are not integer points and lie on no outer border line, counted in both arms

paired_rule_note: pass_rule is retained for gate parser validation; the registered verdict uses totals with accept=no-regress
keep_rule: N06's accept rule for (b) fixes: a batch is accepted when the hard guards hold, no board regresses by more than twice its noise band and the total is not worse than the set's noise; a neutral fix stays in. If the verdict pair passes, N06.13 turns both switches off in ENHANCED through N05
accept: Unit and invariant tests pin both behaviours of both switches (tests/cutout_invariant.rs: java_breaks_the_invariant_outside_the_two_rows, all_fixed_cutouts_tile_the_rest_on_the_extended_set, java_breaks_the_extended_set_through_each_switch).
On the two 45 degree rows every arm's sessions equal the baseline's and both reach counters are 0.
The verdict pair passes the totals rule (no-regress) with the hard and guard metrics.
Grade canary-pwr through the KiCad plugin path; no new real DRC, via-in-pad or below-minimum errors.
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board; no reruns with other settings. No heavy run by the implementer.
